# Rethinking Epicenter's file-editing API I couldn't read the Clarify thread because thread tools aren't available here. Everything below comes from the frozen snapshot. In that snapshot the nested proposal is already in place. `edit-owner.ts:141-145` defines `BufferSnapshot` as `unread | loading | unavailable | ready{text, unsaved?}`, and `Unsaved` is `dirty | saving | failed | conflict` (`:123-126`). All four apps consume it. ## Answer to the central question > **No. The five statuses are not one value. They are three independent facts, and each fact is a small union with its own payload.** Your hypothesis holds, with one refinement: **"conflict" is not a save status at all.** It describes how stored content relates to the source this editor last observed (the witness). A refresh can find it without any save running, and typing doesn't clear it. The current code already shows the compression in several places: - **Newer typing is labelled as saving.** `submitText` copies `saving: input?.pending.saving` onto the new input (`edit-owner.ts:1152`). Text that has never been sent shows as "saving". - **An older revision's failure disappears.** `drain` keeps the failure only if the revision is unchanged (or it was a conflict). Otherwise it drops the error and immediately tries the newer revision (`:860`, `:871-872`). - **Unrelated errors share one field.** `BufferIssue` merges command refusals, read failures, deletion and save errors, picking one by priority (`refusalOf(state) ?? state.error ?? sourceIssue`, `:573`). - **Apps rebuild the missing facts themselves.** Whispering computes `isSaving = unsaved && !failed` from the folder-wide aggregate (`whispering.svelte.ts:1039-1042`). That treats "waiting for the pause" as "saving". - **Callers keep their own copy after a deletion.** `FileEditor.svelte` keeps `lastShown` so the text survives an outside deletion (`:55-64`). ## The proposal: an editor, not a buffer inside an edit ```ts // Acquisition is async. The editor is synchronous memory whose text always exists. folder.files.open(path, schema?): Promise> type TextEditor = { readonly path: string; readonly state: EditorState; // immutable snapshot, replaced on change readonly markdown: MarkdownContent; // schema view of state.text, cached per schema subscribe(listener: () => void): () => void; replaceText(text: string): Result; change(change: DocumentChange): Result; // turns into replaceText save(): Promise>; resolve(d: Divergence, choice: 'mine' | 'theirs' | { text: string }): Promise>; discard(): string; // drops held input and returns its text release(): void; // [Symbol.dispose] }; type EditorState = { text: string; revision: number; // bumps on every accepted change storage: // how text relates to the witness | { kind: 'saved' } | { kind: 'unsaved' } | { kind: 'diverged' } & Divergence; saving?: { revision: number }; // the one write in flight failure?: { revision: number; error: SaveFailure }; // latest attempt that failed refreshFailure?: ReadError; // latest read failed; text is unaffected locked?: { reason: string }; // a fenced action holds the path }; type Divergence = { theirs: { kind: 'text'; text: string } | { kind: 'missing' } | { kind: 'binary' } }; ``` The folder still owns one buffer per path. `open` on a path that is already held resolves without reading. `release` gives up the view's lease. Input that is unsaved or diverged stays with the folder after the view unmounts. Folder ownership and async acquisition remain separate decisions: only `open` is asynchronous. ### Definitions - **Witness.** The exact stored content this editor last reconciled with. Every write is a compare-and-swap against it. - **Saved.** Storage is known to hold exactly `text` (text equals the witness), and no write is running that could change that. - **Dirty (`unsaved`).** Not saved, and storage is not known to have moved. Autosave will run after the pause. - **Diverged.** A read or a rejected write saw stored content that differs from the witness while the editor held input. It also applies after any outside deletion. Autosave stops and `save()` writes nothing. This is the guarantee against silent overwrites. - **Attempt.** One compare-and-swap write of one revision's text. This is what `saving.revision` and `failure.revision` refer to. - **`save()` / flush.** These are one operation. It skips the pause and targets **R, the revision current when it was called**. It resolves `Ok({revision})` when storage holds R or something newer. The returned revision is the one that actually landed, which can be newer than R if typing continued before an attempt started. It resolves `Err` with the failure of the attempt covering R, or with `Diverged`. It does not wait for typing that arrives after the call. `folder.flush()` does the same for every held path and replaces `settle()`. - **Failure lifetime.** A failure applies to its revision and stays until (a) a later attempt settles, which clears or replaces it, or (b) the text becomes saved. **A retry keeps the failure while it runs**, so `saving` and `failure` can both be set. Divergence clears any failure, because the compare-and-swap precondition is already known to be false. ### What callers can count on | Concept | Guarantee | |---|---| | `text: string` | A view never branches on undefined. Deletion can't take the text away. | | `revision` | Results and failures say exactly which text they concern. | | `storage` | Answers "is it safe to close?" and "will autosave run?" | | `saving.revision` | Shows whether the write in flight is older than what's on screen. | | `failure.revision` | Says whether the error is about this text or an earlier one. | | `Divergence` token | Resolution applies to exactly the source that was observed. If storage moved again, it is refused. | ## The sequences **Typing during a save.** The witness is A and the write of r5 (text B) is in flight; the user types r6 (C). - State becomes `unsaved, saving{5}`. The UI can say "Saving… newer changes wait." - If r5 lands, the witness becomes B and r6 autosaves over B. - If r5 fails, the state is `failure{5}` and r6 autosaves after the pause. While r6 is in flight the state is `saving{6}, failure{5}`. When r6 settles, the failure clears or is replaced. **Reverting while a save runs.** The witness is A, r5 (B) is in flight, and the user reverts to r6 = A. - State is `unsaved`, because the outcome is still open. - If r5 lands, the witness is B, A ≠ B, so r6 writes A. Storage briefly holds B; that is the cost of a write that can't be cancelled. - If r5 fails, the witness is still A and equals the text, so the state is `saved`. The failure is dropped because it concerned text nobody holds any more. - This matches the snapshot's two-write path (`:874-885`). The difference is that the state no longer claims the reverted text is "saving". **Retrying a failure.** The state is `failure{5}`; the user calls `save()`. - State becomes `saving{5}, failure{5}`, so the UI can show "Retrying…" without the message flickering away. - On success both clear and the state is `saved`. - On failure, `failure{5}` carries the new error. - Autosave never retries the same revision by itself. New typing does schedule a new attempt. **Typing after a conflict.** The state is `diverged{theirs}`; the user types r7. - Typing is accepted and the state stays diverged, because the divergence belongs to the witness, not the text. - `save()` returns `Err(Diverged)`. - `resolve(d, 'mine')` makes `theirs` the new witness and autosaves r7 over it, still with compare-and-swap. - `'theirs'` replaces the text and gives `saved`. - `{text: merged}` rebases onto theirs and saves the merged text. - If storage moved again, `d` is stale and the call is refused. **A refresh fails.** Only `refreshFailure` is set. Text, `storage` and autosave are unchanged, since a write has its own guard. The next successful read clears it. **A refresh finds the file deleted.** - *With unsaved input:* `diverged{missing}`. "Restore" is `'mine'`, which creates the file. "Discard" is `discard()` plus closing the view. - *Clean:* this is where "text always exists" costs something. A clean editor quietly follows an outside *change*, but it cannot follow a deletion and still have text. So a **clean deletion also becomes `diverged{missing}`**. The last stored text stays visible and nothing autosaves; it would be wrong to bring the file back silently. `'theirs'` on a missing (or binary) source ends the editor: it is released and the result says `ended: true`. - This asymmetry is deliberate. It replaces `lastShown`, `SourceUnavailable`-while-ready and the "deleted elsewhere" branches in all four apps. **Memory versus crash recovery.** `saved` means the compare-and-swap write committed to folder storage. Keeping held input in memory survives unmounts, failures and conflicts, but not a crash or reload. A crash-recovery journal would be a separate folder feature. The editor contract makes no durability claim beyond `saved`. ## Vanilla use ```ts const opened = await folder.files.open('notes/a.md'); if (opened.error) return show(opened.error); // NotFound | NotText | ReadFailed using editor = opened.data; editor.replaceText('# Hello'); const off = editor.subscribe(() => render(editor.state)); const saved = await editor.save(); // Ok({ revision: 1 }) if (saved.error?.name === 'Diverged') { const s = editor.state; if (s.storage.kind === 'diverged') await editor.resolve(s.storage, 'mine'); } ``` ## Svelte The parent handles acquisition. Loading and "not found / not text" move out of the editing component: ```svelte {#key path} {#await folder.files.open(path, NoteSchema)} {:then opened} {#if opened.error} {:else}{/if} {/await} {/key} ``` ```svelte

{#if s.storage.kind === 'diverged'}Changed elsewhere {:else if s.saving}Saving{s.saving.revision < s.revision ? ' (newer changes wait)' : ''}… {:else if s.failure}Not saved: {s.failure.error.message} {:else if s.storage.kind === 'unsaved'}Unsaved {:else}Saved{/if}

{#if s.storage.kind === 'diverged'} {@const d = s.storage} {@const gone = d.theirs.kind !== 'text'} {gone ? 'This note was deleted elsewhere.' : 'This note changed elsewhere.'} {:else if s.failure && !s.saving} {/if} {#if s.refreshFailure}

Couldn't check for outside changes. Your text is kept.

{/if} note.fields.title, (t) => toast(editor.change({ fields: { title: t } }))} disabled={!!s.locked} />
